program_overview.title: AI Tools Mastery for Teens
program_overview.tagline: Every teen already uses AI. This course turns using into understanding: prompting that actually works, tools that are actually allowed at their age, and a real project at the end.
program_overview.description:
AI is already in every teenager’s day, in search, homework, music and feeds, usually unexamined and often against the tools’ own age rules. This live online course for ages 13 to 18 replaces that drift with skill: how AI actually works, prompting as a craft, AI art and media created with tools that genuinely permit teens, AI as a study partner used ethically, coding assistants, training small machine-learning models, and a capstone project that combines them.

Age honesty is a feature of this course, not a footnote: every tool taught is selected for 13+ availability, accounts are set up together with a parent where consent is required, and the course explicitly teaches which popular tools teens should NOT be using yet and why. Ethics runs throughout: hallucinations and fact-checking from week 2, academic honesty in the study weeks, bias, privacy and deepfake awareness before graduation.

The pace is honest: 4 months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of practice, with a fifth month in hand for teens who want more time. Homework follows every class, each month ends with a mixed challenge that revisits earlier skills, and the course ends with a final exam, a capstone demo plus written questions, that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision. Real skill, real judgment, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Age-clean by design: every tool taught genuinely permits teens, accounts are set up with parents, and the course teaches which famous tools are off-limits until 18 and why
Prompting taught as a craft: structure, context, iteration and evaluation, not magic phrases
Ethics is load-bearing: fact-checking, academic honesty, bias, privacy and deepfake awareness are core weeks, not disclaimers
Beyond chatting: teens train their own small ML models and use AI coding assistants, the builder’s side of AI
An honest 4-month arc with a fifth month in hand: nobody is rushed, nobody coasts
Real assessment: weekly homework, monthly mixed challenges, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest

faqs.question: What age is appropriate for this AI tools course?
faqs.answer: Ages 13 to 18. That floor is deliberate: the major AI platforms themselves require 13+ with parental consent, and this course treats those rules as part of the curriculum. Younger children learn AI concepts hands-on in our kids coding course instead, using classroom-safe tools like Machine Learning for Kids and Teachable Machine.

faqs.question: Is it safe for my teenager to use AI tools?
faqs.answer: With the right setup and habits, yes, and building those habits is half this course. Accounts are created together with a parent wherever consent is required, no personal information goes into prompts, outputs are fact-checked as a reflex, and the course explicitly covers hallucinations, bias, privacy and deepfake awareness. Your teen also learns which popular tools are 18+ and why waiting matters.

faqs.question: How long does the course take?
faqs.answer: Four months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of practice, with a fifth month in hand for teens who want more time on the builder skills, no rushing and no penalty. The course is paced so every week produces something real: a portfolio piece, a study system, a trained model, and it ends with a capstone exam.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Homework follows every class, each month ends with a mixed challenge that revisits earlier tools and adds ethics questions, and the course ends with a final exam: a capstone demo plus a written paper covering the whole syllabus, including tool-age judgment. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest. Real skill and real judgment, not attendance.

faqs.question: Will my teenager learn actual skills or just play with AI toys?
faqs.answer: Actual skills, in layers: prompt engineering practiced against rubrics, ethical research and study workflows, AI-assisted creative production with honest crediting, coding assistants, and training small machine-learning models of their own. The capstone requires combining tools into one defended project. Toys do not survive a viva.

faqs.question: Which AI tools does the course use, and are they allowed for teens?
faqs.answer: Only tools that genuinely permit ages 13+ (with parental consent where required): ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Adobe Firefly, Canva AI, Bing Image Creator, GitHub Copilot, Teachable Machine and similar. Some well-known tools, several art generators and voice-cloning services among them, are 18+ by their own terms, and the course teaches exactly that instead of quietly ignoring it. Our public AI tools age guide lists every tool’s floor.

faqs.question: Will this help with school, or make cheating easier?
faqs.answer: It is built to help honestly. The study weeks teach AI as a tutor and research partner: explaining concepts, generating practice questions, checking reasoning, always with verification and always inside school policy. Academic honesty is taught explicitly, including what crosses the line and why detection is the least of the reasons not to.

faqs.question: What equipment does my teenager need?
faqs.answer: A computer or laptop with a stable internet connection. The course runs on free tiers of every tool; where an account needs parental consent, it is set up together in the first weeks. No paid subscriptions are required for the syllabus.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 students. A mini batch of 3-4 students is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Parents are welcome to sit in, and the age-and-safety setup is explained right there.

faqs.answer: Live, always: small interactive groups with a real instructor, never pre-recorded videos. AI tools change monthly, and live teaching is the only format that keeps up honestly.

why_this_course.title: Why Teens Need AI Skill, Not Just AI Access
paragraphs: Every teenager already has AI access; almost none have AI skill. The difference shows up everywhere: in study quality, in what they believe online, in the projects they can build, and in whether they respect the age rules the platforms themselves set. Skill is teachable, and it compounds.

This course teaches the full stack of AI literacy: prompting as a craft, creation with tools teens are actually allowed to use, ethical study workflows, the builder’s layer of coding assistants and self-trained models, and the judgment to know what to trust. Age honesty is a feature throughout, the course names the 18+ tools and explains the waiting.

It ends the way real learning should: a capstone project combining several tools, defended at demo day, and a final exam that decides the certificate. Four months, honestly paced, with a fifth in hand.
